business_patterns.top_pattern: Authorization classification and mapping shifts must be validated before action
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: Commercial Local Group inpatient spend affected by PA classification and facility mapping changes

providers: OHIO STATE UNIVERSITY WEXNER MEDICAL CENTER

key_driver_codes: Postpartum and Postabortion Diagnoses without O.R. Procedures
business_patterns.pattern_details: A large share of the observed spend change is tied to shifts in PA-required classification and one unmapped facility bucket rather than a confirmed change in demand or reimbursement. The signal is concentrated in NY, CT, and CA / GA / OH / VA, with the biggest provider concentrations at NYU Langone and Yale New Haven. Business action on utilization or contracting should wait until the PA and facility mapping logic is reconciled.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: If the PA or facility fields moved, the organization could misdirect UM and reimbursement actions at the wrong providers or products.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Reconcile AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION and Not Mapped claims to source PA-required and facility type logic in CT, NY, and CA / GA / OH / VA, then rerun provider and product comparisons before taking UM or reimbursement action.
business_patterns.validation_reason: Multiple groups are explicitly flagged for auth or mapping shift and require validation before action.
evidence_summary: NY AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION added about $3.9M, led by NYU Langone at $2.7M and cervical spinal fusion with CC at $1.1M.
CT AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION added about $2.8M and is concentrated at Yale New Haven.
CA / GA / OH / VA AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION was net +$2.5M, led by IU Health Methodist at $1.1M and Henrico at $1.0M, with some offsetting negatives.
A CA PPO Not Mapped facility bucket added about $161K, indicating facility classification cleanup is also needed.

business_patterns.top_pattern: CT PPO acute hospital spend is concentrated at Yale with both more admissions and higher paid per admit
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CT PPO acute hospital inpatient spend
key_driver_codes: Other Digestive System Diagnoses with MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: CT PPO acute hospital spend rose sharply at Yale New Haven Hospital, with pressure coming from both PA-required and non-PA cases. This is not a pure utilization story: admissions increased and paid per admit also moved higher. The mix suggests a combined UM and reimbursement issue rather than a single lever.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A single provider concentration of this size can materially move CT inpatient cost trend and needs a targeted response.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Open a joint UM and network review on Yale CT PPO acute admissions, focusing on PA routing, admission criteria, level of care, and reimbursement terms for the highest-cost digestive cases.
business_patterns.validation_reason: Both PA-required and non-PA claims contributed materially at the same provider, so PA flag assignment should be confirmed alongside utilization and rate review.
evidence_summary: Yale New Haven PA-required PPO acute cases added about $3.8M with 38 more admissions and roughly $9K higher paid per admit.
Yale non-PA PPO acute cases added about $0.8M with 43 more admissions and roughly $3K higher paid per admit.
Other Digestive System Diagnoses with MCC added about $235K on 4 admissions with roughly $59K higher paid per admit.

business_patterns.top_pattern: NY EPO acute hospital pressure is concentrated at NYU Langone and spine surgery
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: NY EPO acute hospital inpatient spend
business_patterns.pattern_details: NY EPO acute hospital spend increased mainly in PA-required cases and is heavily concentrated at NYU Langone. The largest identifiable clinical driver is cervical spinal fusion, where the case count and paid per admit both rose. This looks like a focused provider and procedure pressure point rather than a broad NY inpatient trend.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Concentrated EPO inpatient growth at one flagship provider can quickly become a recurring cost issue if not addressed early.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Run a provider-level inpatient audit at NYU Langone for PA-required EPO admissions, pairing medical-necessity review with reimbursement review for cervical fusion and other high-cost surgical stays.
business_patterns.validation_reason: A meaningful share of the increase is concentrated in low-volume surgical cells, so PA status and claim classification should be confirmed before broader contract action.
evidence_summary: NYU Langone added about $2.8M in PA-required EPO acute cases with 25 more admissions and roughly $31K higher paid per admit.
Cervical spinal fusion with CC added about $379K on 5 admissions with roughly $76K higher paid per admit.
One IU Health Methodist case added about $244K but is a single-admission outlier.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Smaller-state provider mix pressure is emerging across PPO and POS inpatient business
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: Acute hospital and childrens inpatient spend across CA, GA, IN, KY, ME, MO, NH, NY, OH, VA

providers: OHIO STATE UNIVERSITY WEXNER MEDICAL CENTER

key_driver_codes: Other Digestive System Diagnoses with MCC

business_patterns.pattern_details: Beyond the largest CT and NY clusters, multiple smaller state and product combinations are showing emerging inpatient pressure tied to provider mix, more admissions, and higher paid per admit. The signal is concentrated at IU Health Methodist, Henrico, NYU Langone, and Ohio State, and most contributors are PA-required or low-baseline cases. This is an early-warning provider economics pattern that can be addressed before it becomes a broader trend.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Small but recurring provider-product spikes can compound quickly and often indicate contract, referral, or pre-service control gaps.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Create a targeted provider-product watchlist for contract review and pre-service controls, prioritizing IU Health Methodist, Henrico, NYU Langone, and Ohio State where paid per admit spiked off small baselines.
business_patterns.validation_reason: Many contributing cells are low-baseline or small-volume, so provider and product configuration should be confirmed before broad repricing or policy changes.
evidence_summary: GA POS acute hospital at IU Health Methodist added about $0.9M with 3 more admissions and roughly $228K higher paid per admit.
VA PPO acute hospital at Henrico added about $0.5M with 2 more admissions and roughly $24K higher paid per admit.
CA PPO acute hospital added about $1.4M across IU Health Methodist, NYU Langone, and Henrico, including both PA-required and non-PA cases.
KY childrens PPO digestive MCC added about $391K on 3 admissions with roughly $130K higher paid per admit.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Several inpatient segments are rising mainly because admissions increased, not because rates worsened
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: PPO and POS acute hospital inpatient utilization across OH, CA, CT, IN, MO, VA, WI

key_driver_codes: Acute Myocardial Infarction, Discharged Alive with CC
Other Digestive System Diagnoses with MCC
Postpartum and Postabortion Diagnoses without O.R. Procedures
business_patterns.pattern_details: A separate set of inpatient increases is primarily volume-led: admissions and claims rose while paid per admit was flat or down in several segments. The clearest examples are Ohio PPO, California PPO, and Virginia POS. This points to UM, referral, and admission management rather than contract rate pressure as the primary lever.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Using network or reimbursement actions on a volume-led problem would miss the main driver and delay savings.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Deploy UM admission review and referral management in the cited acute hospital segments, especially AMI, digestive, and postpartum admissions where counts rose while paid per admit stayed flat or fell.
evidence_summary: OH PPO acute hospital at Ohio State added about $0.8M with 23 more admissions while paid per admit fell about $6K.
CA PPO acute hospital utilization added about $487K across digestive, AMI, and postpartum DRGs, with flat to down unit cost.
VA POS acute hospital at Henrico added about $201K with 23 more admissions and paid per admit down about $8K.
IN / WI POS and CT / MO PPO added another roughly $383K, largely from AMI-related admissions growth.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Rare high-cost IP Med/Surg cases are creating outsized spend swings
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: IP Med/Surg rare high-cost surgical and complex medical cases in NY and CA / GA / OH / VA

providers: OHIO STATE UNIVERSITY WEXNER MEDICAL CENTER

key_driver_codes: Coronary Bypass without Cardiac Catheterization with MCC
Cardiac Valve and Other Major Cardiothoracic Procedures without Cardiac Catheterization with MCC
Wound Debridement and Skin Graft Except Hand for Musculoskeletal and Connective Tissue Disorders with MCC
Other Digestive System Diagnoses with MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: This is a focused outlier case-mix pattern, not a broad inpatient trend. Spend is being driven by a small number of rare, very high-cost IP Med/Surg cases across NY and CA / GA / OH / VA, frequently with only 1 to 3 admissions and six-figure paid per admit. The main business need is case-level clinical and outlier management, not broad benefit or policy changes.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A handful of rare surgical or complex medical cases can distort trend and require a different response than routine utilization growth.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Route these episodes to case-level clinical and outlier review to confirm DRG and diagnosis accuracy, assess stop-loss or catastrophic exposure, and separate one-time events from repeatable management opportunities.
business_patterns.validation_reason: Most contributing cases are small-volume, low-baseline events with unusually high paid per admit.
evidence_summary: NY rare IP Med/Surg outliers added about $2.6M, including ulcer of intestine digestive MCC at about $469K and coronary bypass at NYU Langone at about $448K.
CA / GA / OH / VA rare IP Med/Surg cases added about $2.5M, led by Ohio State wound debridement and skin graft at about $401K and cardiothoracic surgery at about $384K.
NY / VA cardiac valve procedures without cath with MCC added about $1.0M across NYU Langone and Henrico.
Most contributing cases involved 1 to 3 admissions with six-figure paid per admit.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Catastrophic airway and transplant episodes need dedicated case management
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: IP Med/Surg catastrophic tracheostomy, prolonged ventilation, sepsis, and transplant cases in CT, GA, VA
key_driver_codes: Tracheostomy with Mechanical Ventilation >96 Hours or Principal Diagnosis Except Face, Mouth and Neck without Major O.R. Procedures
business_patterns.pattern_details: A small number of catastrophic airway and transplant episodes generated very large spend increases across Yale, Henrico, and IU Health Methodist. These are specialized cases with extremely high paid per admit and very low volumes, so they need individual case handling rather than broad utilization policy changes. The presence of tracheostomy with prolonged ventilation and transplant cases points to the need for catastrophic case management and contract carve-out review.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Catastrophic cases can overwhelm normal trend management and often depend on specialized clinical, authorization, and reimbursement workflows.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Launch case-level review for tracheostomy, prolonged ventilation, sepsis, and kidney transplant episodes, including catastrophic case management, transplant authorization, and contract carve-out validation.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The increases are driven by rare, small-count cases with very high paid per admit.
evidence_summary: Yale New Haven tracheostomy with prolonged ventilation and sepsis added about $1.4M across 2 admissions, or about $702K paid per admit.
IU Health Methodist added about $509K from a single tracheostomy-related case.
Kidney transplant cases in GA / VA added about $441K across 2 admissions at Henrico and IU Health Methodist.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Maternity and NICU acuity is emerging through C-section-linked neonatal severity and maternal complications
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: IP NICU and IP OB delivery/well newborn maternity spend in GA, VA, NY
key_driver_codes: Extreme Immaturity or Respiratory Distress Syndrome, Neonate
business_patterns.pattern_details: Maternity-related acuity is showing up through NICU respiratory distress and extreme prematurity in GA / VA, plus severe pre-eclampsia in NY. The largest concentration is at Henrico, where neonatal cases tied to C-section births drove most of the increase. This is a focused maternity and newborn severity pattern that warrants OB and NICU review, not a broad inpatient response.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Maternal and neonatal high-acuity cases have different clinical and care-management levers than general Med/Surg utilization.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Conduct a combined OB and NICU review of maternal complications and neonatal respiratory distress, with focus on C-section-linked NICU severity and opportunities for maternity case management.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The pattern is concentrated in small numbers of high-acuity maternity and neonatal admissions.
evidence_summary: GA / VA NICU extreme immaturity or respiratory distress added about $636K, led by Henrico at about $503K across 4 admissions tied to C-section births.
NY severe pre-eclampsia in IP OB delivery/well newborn added about $38K across 2 admissions.
These are low-volume but high-acuity maternity and newborn cases rather than a broad obstetric utilization shift.

executive_summary.headline: The biggest actionable story is that several large inpatient increases sit behind authorization classification shifts, while the confirmed cost pressure is concentrated in a small set of acute hospital providers and rare high-cost cases.
executive_summary.primary_business_message: First, validate PA and facility mapping because roughly $9.3M of apparent impact is tied to AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION or unmapped classification movement. After that gate, the clearest provider-mix pressure sits at Yale New Haven in CT PPO and NYU Langone in NY EPO, with both admissions and paid per admit rising. A second tier of multistate provider spikes, utilization-led admission growth, and rare catastrophic clinical outliers should then be routed to the right UM, network, and clinical teams.
recommended_focus_order: Validate AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION and Not Mapped facility logic before acting on spend signals
Target Yale New Haven CT PPO and NYU Langone NY EPO acute hospital pressure with joint UM and reimbursement action
Address the remaining multistate provider spikes, utilization-led admission growth, and rare catastrophic clinical outliers through targeted case and contract review

notes: All AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION groups were consolidated into one gating validation pattern, and the CA Not Mapped facility signal was folded into the same validation story.
Operational acute hospital findings were split into provider-concentrated mixed pressure, emerging smaller-state provider mix, and pure utilization growth because the business levers differ.
A small number of lower-impact niche clinical groups were left ungrouped to preserve clear business actions within the 8-pattern limit.
Left 4 analytical groups unassigned to preserve clean narrative attribution.
